newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes flat amid cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes flat amid cautious trade.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 345-355 per dollar, almost flat from 350-355 in the morning, amid thin interbank trade afte the central bank said it would take steps to prevent a further sharp lev fall, dealers said.
"Market activity was very low because most traders were cautious after the central bank said it would act to counter speculative pressure on the lev," a commercial bank dealer said.

The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Friday it had agreed to coordinated action with commercial banks to prevent further sharp falls in the lev, which slumped from 275 to 395 per dollar last week due to a dollar rush.
As a result, many financial houses were denied buying foreign currency from banks on Monday, which tamed cash market trade, another dealer said.
However, brokerages were able to sell foreign currency to banks, the dealer said.
The BNB also said on Friday it had curbed liquidity in banks, brokerages and foreign exchange bureaus but did not elaborate. Details on the curbs were not available.
"These statements have had a strong psychological effect on the market, and we saw more final clients offering dollars today," a third dealer said.
The central bank took advantage of the rise in dollar supply and bought light foreign currency volumes around 350-352 levs, dealers said.

Loss of confidence in the lev and rumours about the negative impact of a currency board, proposed by the International Monetary Fund to stabilise the economy, sparked panic among Bulgarians last week.
They rushed to convert their savings into hard currency, fearing they might lose their deposits and treasury paper investments under a currency board system.
The lev hit the a record low of 395 per dollar on the interbank market and 420 on the cash market on Thursday.
